title: Dependency Injection
description: InversifyJS and DI patterns for TypeScript.

data.text: Dependency Injection (DI) decouples object creation from usage. InversifyJS is a powerful DI container for TypeScript.

data.title: InversifyJS setup

data.text: Dependency injection means a class receives what it needs instead of constructing it. That removes the hard-wired `new Database()` inside a service and lets a test pass a fake. In TypeScript, the interface is what the consumer depends on; the implementation is supplied by the caller.

data.title: Constructor injection with an interface

data.text: A DI container resolves a graph of dependencies from registrations, so application code asks for a service and the container builds it. NestJS and Angular ship with one. The benefit is that wiring lives in one place; the cost is indirection that is harder to follow and errors that appear at runtime rather than compile time.

data.title: Registering providers
Interview angle: DI is for testability, not for magic
data.text: The reason to inject a dependency is that you can substitute it, which makes tests fast and isolated and lets configuration choose an implementation. A container is optional: constructor injection by hand covers most applications. When asked, explain the inversion and the testing benefit first, and treat the container as one way to assemble the graph.
